newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: S.Lanka rupee ends barely moved on high dlr supply.
newsitem.headline: S.Lanka rupee ends barely moved on high dlr supply.

text.p: The Sri Lanka rupee closed little moved against the dollar on Tuesday in a market well supplied with the U.S. currency, dealers said.
The rupee closed at 58.89 to the dollar after opening at 58.88.
"There were some trade-backed transactions today but there were enough dollars to keep the exchange rate stable," said an American Express Bank dealer.
The central bank pushed down the dollar by three-quarters of a local cent, fixing buying and selling prices at 58.8728 and 60.0622.
Dealers said Tuesday's announcement that Japan's NTT had paid $225 million dollars for 35 percent of state-owned Sri Lanka Telecom would not have an impact on the exchange rate.
"The inflow will not have an impact on the exchange rate, since NTT will pay the money to the Treasury in dollars," said a HongKong Bank dealer.
"Also, the downside is limited because the exchange rate is already close to the central bank's bottom," he added.
Overnight call money closed at 8.875 percent after opening at nine, due to two state banks lending, dealers said.
